On the multipole mixing ratio of the 365 keV γ-transition in 129Ba
S. Chakraborty∗
Experimental Nuclear Physics Division, Physics Group,
Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre, Kolkata, India.
The E2/M1 multipole mixing ratio (δ), reported by J. Gizon et al. [Phys. Rev. C 17, 596 (1978)],
for 365 keV γ-transition in 129Ba is reevaluated and found altered.
Experimentally determined
angular distribution coefficients indicate a large E2 admixture in the 365 keV γ-ray. Indeed, it is
found in better agreement with the reported linear polarization value for this γ-ray.
In Ref. [1], J. Gizon and co-workers measured the an-
gular distribution and linear polarization of some γ-rays
in 129Ba.
In particular, for 365 keV γ-transition, the
following spectroscopic results were reported:
A22 = – 0.70 (3); A44 = 0.16 (5); P = 0.072 (68)
Based on the angular distribution (linear polarization)
results, the multipole mixing ratio −0.97 ⩽δ ⩽−0.79
(−0.84 ⩽δ ⩽−0.31) was determined for this γ-ray and
finally, an effective value of −0.84 ⩽δ ⩽−0.79 was
adopted. However, the experimentally measured linear
polarization also satisfies a higher magnitude of δ, as
shown in the FIG. 2 of Ref. [1].
